members.claim: This conversion changes how every bivariate layer is coloured. The old renderer classified the raw ratio numerator/denominator against `legend.axis.{x,y}.steps`, which are in raw data units. The new style builds MCDA score and base dimensions (`createMCDALayersFromBivariateAxes`), and `createBivariateMultivariateStyle` turns them into normalized max-min values (roughly 0..1, using the sigma range or transformation). Those normalized values are then classified against `stepOverrides` set to the raw axis steps. The units don't match: for example, population density steps of 0/10/100… compared with values in 0..1 put nearly every hexagon in the first class. The fill filter also changes from `filterSetup` to `mcdaFilterSetup`. The unit test only checks the object's shape, so it can't catch this.

members.claim: Keep axis calculations in the same units as legend thresholds
members.evidence: `createMCDALayersFromBivariateAxes` enables max-min normalization, clamping, and potentially sentiment inversion, but these overrides retain the original axis thresholds. The multivariate style compares normalized scores against those raw thresholds, so an axis with thresholds such as 10 and 100 will classify every score in the lowest bucket instead of preserving the original bivariate colors. Popup cell classification has the same mismatch. Preserve the original axis-value semantics or convert the thresholds consistently with the score calculation.

members.claim: The tile source max zoom regresses. The old code used `getMaxNumeratorZoomLevel(legend quotients)` for bivariate layers and `getMaxMCDAZoomLevel(style.config)` for MCDA layers. The new code inherits `MultivariateRenderer.getMaxZoomLevel`, which reads `layer.style` from the tile source, not the converted state style. members.claim: Pass the converted style through to source zoom calculation
members.evidence: When a source has no explicit `maxZoom`, the inherited `MultivariateRenderer.getMaxZoomLevel` inspects `state.source.style`, not `state.style`.
